transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess the main thing is… work’s been getting a little harder to keep straight. I’m an electrician, and lately I can’t seem to stay focused on one estimate or code form long enough. Like, a tool noise, or a text, or even some idea I get about the workshop will pull me off, and then I come back and jobs are kind of mixed up. I’m trying to stay on top of it, but it’s gotten frustrating enough that I figured I should probably talk to someone.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it fidgeting exactly, but sitting still feels kind of useless lately. I’ve been keeping myself moving—job sites, then bids, then back in the workshop rewiring test panels or starting some home-automation idea before I’ve even finished the last one. It’s productive, sort of, but… yeah, I guess I do feel pretty restless when I’m not doing something. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are you having trouble meeting deadlines or fulfilling responsibilities at work due to your difficulty staying focused?

A little, yeah. I mean, I’m still getting the work done for the most part, but clients have started pointing out missed details, and I’ve mixed up scheduling more than I’d like to admit. My apprentices seem less confident following my direction lately, which… doesn’t feel great.

And at home it’s become a thing too. My wife’s worried about the mortgage and the business, and we’ve been arguing because she feels like I’m putting what we built at risk. I don’t think I’m trying to be careless, but I can see why it looks that way.
Have you been feeling anxious or overwhelmed by your work situation or anything else lately?

I mean… overwhelmed maybe a little, yeah, but I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t handle my job. It’s more like there’s just a lot coming at me, and I’m trying to keep everything moving without letting people down.

Anxious… I’m not sure if that’s the right word. I get stressed when things pile up or my wife brings up the business stuff, but I figure that’s kind of normal, right?
Have you been acting on impulse more often lately?

I’m not sure… maybe a little? I wouldn’t say I’m doing anything wild, at least I don’t think so. Sometimes I make quick calls because it feels like the right thing in the moment, especially with work stuff, but I usually have a reason for it.

What do you mean by impulse exactly—like spending money or picking fights, or just making decisions fast?
Have you been more argumentative or short-tempered with family or friends lately?

Yeah… I guess I have been a little sharper than usual. I don’t mean to be. It’s not like I’m trying to pick fights or anything.

Sometimes I’ll get really fired up talking about where the shop could go, like we could really become the main solar outfit around here, and I’m kind of energized about it. But then if my wife or one of the apprentices pushes back or questions the plan, I can… snap a bit. Get short with them over stuff that probably isn’t that big a deal.

I know that doesn’t sound great. I’m working on catching myself, but yeah, I think they’d probably say I’ve been more argumentative.
Do you find yourself easily distracted by things around you when you're not at work?

Yeah… I mean, I do get pulled off track more than I’d like. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely scattered, but it’s been noticeable.

Even when I’m not actively on a job, if I’m trying to sit down with an estimate or a code form, something small will pull me away — a tool noise, a text coming in, or I’ll suddenly get this idea about the workshop and think, “Oh, I should write that down,” and then I’m off on that instead.

And then I come back and realize I mixed something up or didn’t finish the first thing. That’s kind of what finally made me think, okay, maybe this is becoming a problem. Does that make sense?
Have you always had trouble staying focused and sitting still, or is this something that's developed more recently?

I don’t think it’s always been like this, no. I mean, I’ve had normal restlessness like anyone, but this feels more recent.

It’s probably been building for… maybe seven months? Around when we took on the mortgage for the workshop and equipment. I kept telling myself it was just the stress of that, which maybe it partly is, but yeah, that’s when I started noticing it more. Does that sound like the kind of timeline you’re asking about?
Would you describe these difficulties with focus and restlessness as something that has been present for as long as you can remember?

No, I wouldn’t say it’s been as long as I can remember. I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s more like it’s been building over the last… about seven months or so, since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and equipment. I kept thinking it was just the pressure of that, which maybe it is partly, but it hasn’t really felt like a lifelong thing. Does that answer what you mean?
Would you say that your difficulties with focus and restlessness are causing problems in your relationships with your wife or others?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say it’s not, but it is starting to.

At work, clients have complained a couple times about details I missed or schedules getting mixed up, and that’s embarrassing. My apprentices have noticed too, I think — they don’t seem to trust my direction the way they used to, which is hard to admit.

And at home… my wife and I argue more than we used to. Mostly about the mortgage and the business stuff. She feels like I’m putting what we built at risk, and I can see why she’d feel that way, even if I’m trying not to. I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart, but yeah, it’s causing problems.
How much distress or upset would you say these difficulties with focus and restlessness are causing you?

I’d say… moderate, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I’m still getting through the day and doing what I need to do, mostly.

But it does bother me. When clients complain about missed details or scheduling getting mixed up, I take that pretty hard. And with my apprentices, feeling like they don’t quite trust my direction the way they used to… that’s upsetting.

At home it’s probably worse emotionally. The mortgage and the business keep turning into arguments, and my wife feels like I’m putting everything we built at risk. I don’t like that at all. So yeah, it’s causing me distress — not completely overwhelming, but definitely more than I’d like. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are you finding it harder to enjoy activities or spend time with family and friends because of your difficulties with focus and restlessness?

Yeah… somewhat. I don’t think it’s that I don’t want to be around my family or anything like that. I still care about all of that.

But it’s harder to enjoy it when my head is on the business, or I’m worrying I missed something. Clients have started complaining about little details and scheduling getting mixed up, and then I bring that stress home. My apprentices don’t seem to trust my direction the way they used to either, which… honestly bothers me more than I’d like to admit.

And at home, the mortgage and the business stuff keep turning into arguments with my wife. She feels like I’m putting what we built at risk. So even when we’re spending time together, it doesn’t always feel relaxed. I don’t know if that answers it right, but yes, it’s getting in the way some.
Would you say that your difficulties with focus and restlessness are significantly interfering with your ability to function in daily life?

Yeah… I think I’d have to say yes, at least to a noticeable degree. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function at all, because I am still working and trying to keep things moving.

But clients have started complaining about details I’ve missed and scheduling getting mixed up, and that’s not like me. My apprentices seem like they don’t trust my direction the way they used to, which is… hard to admit.

And at home, the mortgage and business stuff keeps turning into arguments with my wife. She feels like I’m putting everything we built at risk. So yeah, I guess it is interfering with daily life more than I’d like. Is that what you mean by significantly?
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feelings of sadness or depression, alongside these difficulties with focus and restlessness?

Not really sadness, no… I wouldn’t call it depression. If anything, it’s kind of the opposite sometimes, which I know maybe sounds better than it is.

I get into these really pumped-up moods, like I’m talking about the shop like we’re about to become the main solar outfit in town. I’ll feel pretty sure of the plan, excited about it. But then if my wife questions it, or one of the apprentices pushes back even a little, I can get… sharper than I mean to. Irritated over things that probably don’t deserve that reaction.

I don’t like admitting that, because I’m not trying to be difficult. But yeah, my mood has been more up and more easily irritated than sad, if that makes sense.
Do you find that you have trouble staying focused and feeling restless both at work and at home?

Yeah… I think it happens in both places, though work is where it’s easiest to see.

I mean, I can still get things done, but what finally made me think I should come in is I can’t seem to stay with one estimate or code form the way I used to. A tool noise, a text coming in, or even some new idea about the workshop will pull me off, and then I realize I’ve jumped to something else and the jobs start getting mixed up.

At home it’s similar, just less obvious maybe. My mind keeps drifting back to the shop or the next thing I should be doing. I don’t want to overstate it, but yes, it’s not just one place. Does that make sense?
Do you experience these difficulties with focus and restlessness during leisure activities or when you're not thinking about work?

I think… mostly it’s tied to work, or at least that’s where I notice it the most. I don’t want to overstate it like I can’t sit still for anything.

But even when I’m not supposed to be working, my head kind of gets pulled back there. What really got me to come in was that I can’t keep my attention on one estimate or one code form the way I used to. A tool noise, a text, or some new idea about the workshop can pull me off track, and then I realize the jobs are getting mixed up.

So leisure time… I guess I don’t separate from it very well. But the clearest problem is still with those work tasks, if that answers what you’re asking.
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity since childhood?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean, I don’t remember being told as a kid that I was unusually hyper or anything like that.

School wasn’t perfect, but I don’t know if I’d call it the same as what’s been happening lately. I don’t want to give you a wrong answer just to make it fit. Maybe my parents would remember better, but from what I can say, I don’t have a clear childhood history of that. Does that help?
Do you think your difficulties with focus and restlessness have been present in some form since you were a child, even if they weren't as noticeable or problematic back then?

I don’t think I can honestly say it goes back to childhood, no. At least, not in a way I clearly remember.

This feels more like something that’s been building over the last several months… maybe about seven months now, since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment. I don’t want to blame everything on that, but that’s when I started noticing it more. Is that the kind of timeline you mean?
Do you think your difficulties with focus and restlessness have been a consistent part of your behavior over the last 6 months?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has been pretty consistent for about seven months now.

It kind of started building after we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment. Since then it’s been there in some form most of the time. Does that answer it the right way?
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity for at least 6 months?

Yes… I think it’s fair to say it’s been at least six months. It’s been building for about seven months now, since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment.

I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s the timeframe I’ve noticed.
